newsitem.title: ISRAEL: EU tries to set Arafat-Levy Mideast peace meeting.
newsitem.headline: EU tries to set Arafat-Levy Mideast peace meeting.

text.p: The European Union is trying to set a meeting between Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy in Brussels next week on ending a Middle East peace deadlock, an EU spokesman said on Thursday.
Israeli and PLO officials confirmed both Levy and Arafat had been invited to a Brussels meeting of EU foreign ministers on July 22 but said a meeting between the two men had not yet been arranged.
"It could lead to a meeting provided there is progress," Kristof Sarnaud, a spokesman for EU Middle East envoy Miguel Moratinos, told Reuters. "We don't want a photo opportunity."

Such a meeting would be the highest Israeli-PLO contact since Arafat and Levy met briefly at a Euro-Mediterranean conference in Malta in April in a highly publicised handshake that failed to achieve a breakthrough.

Israeli-PLO peace moves have been in crisis and the West Bank and Gaza rocked by unrest since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sent bulldozers in March to an Arab East Jerusalem hillside to build thousands of Jewish homes.
Moratinos held talks with Levy and Arafat on Wednesday and continued to shuttle on Thursday between senior Israeli and Palestinian officials.

The European initiative comes as Egyptian efforts to mediate a package of Israeli-PLO confidence building measures edged forward. The United States, the main sponsor of Middle East peace talks, has lowered its mediation profile.

Mohammad Bassiouny, Egypt's ambassador to Israel, said after a meeting between Israel's defence chief and PLO offcial at his home on Wednesday night that the sides wanted to reach agreement on an airport to serve Palestinians in the self-ruled Gaza Strip "as soon as possible".
Sarnaud said Europe hoped Levy would bring a "significant political gesture" to Brussels to help pave the way for a meeting with Arafat.

Neither Israel nor the PLO ruled out a Levy-Arafat meeting but Israel repeated its charge that Palestinian violence was the main obstacle to progress. The PLO held firm to its stance that the peace crisis stemmed from Israeli settlement building.
"In spite of the Israeli-Palestinian contacts and all the Egyptian and European efforts, no real progress has been achieved until now," Arafat's aide Nabil Abu Rdaineh told Reuters.
"We hold Israel responsible for the escalation of tensions in the region..Israel is still insisting to go ahead with settlement activities," Abu Rdaineh said.

Abu Rdaineh called on Israel to respect Tuesday's U.N. General Assembly resolution condemning the Jewish state for building settlements in occupied areas. Israel rejected the resolution as "shameful" and "morally bankrupt".

Levy kept the public gaze focused on Israel's arrest of three Palestinian police officers Israel said were on their way to launch a shooting attack on a Jewish settlement near the PLO-ruled city of Nablus on the West Bank on Monday. The army on Wednesday said it had arrested a fourth Palestinian officer.

"It is certain that peace will not advance by pressure, threats, incitement or violence," Levy told reporters in Jerusalem. "The fact...that Palestinian police worked to carry out attacks is very very serious."
Levy said he had received a response to a message he sent to Arafat on the issue. "The Authority understands the severity and will deal with it," the foreign minister said.

Asked whether a meeting with Arafat in Brussels could mark a breakthrough in restarting peace talks, Levy replied: "Very possibly...(but) one thing must be clear. The process will get back on track on a completely different code of character."

The trial opened on Thursday of an Israeli woman accused of putting up posters in Hebron depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig and adjourned for two weeks so she could undergo psychiatric examination.
The posters, pasted on June 27 across 20 storefronts on the Palestinian-ruled side of the West Bank town, provoked an oupouring of Moslem ire and violent anti-Israeli protests.
